tool2.limit: Size and industry affect context, support and penalty calculations, but do not create a general exemption.
tool2.smeHelp: An SME usually has fewer than 250 employees and meets the EU financial test. Ownership links can change this.
tool2.midcapHelp: A small mid-cap is not an SME, has fewer than 750 employees and meets the financial ceiling. Ownership still matters.
tool2.officialChecker: Use the Commission's detailed beta checker

sources.title: Official sources and change history
sources.intro: The guide uses one dated source register. It keeps the original publication, language-specific corrections, later amendments and non-binding guidance separate.
sources.originalBody: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 was published in the Official Journal on 12 July 2024. The archived English PDF is the authentic publication. The English XHTML is stored to support structured references. The metadata XML identifies all 24 language editions but contains no body of the law.
sources.currentBody: The project's explanation is a dated reading of the original act together with the corrections and amendments identified below. It is not an official consolidated text. The project will only call a consolidation official when EUR-Lex publishes it as such.
sources.timelineTitle: Application timeline used by this guide
sources.timelineItems: 2 August 2026 — most general rules and Article 50 apply.
2 December 2026 — new Article 5 provisions introduced by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 apply.
2 December 2026 — narrow Article 50(2) provider-marking transition ends for relevant generative systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026.
2 December 2027 — relevant Annex III high-risk provisions apply.
2 August 2028 — relevant Annex I product-related high-risk provisions apply.
sources.archiveBody: Each archived item records its official URL, retrieval time in UTC, byte count and SHA-256 checksum. Automated checks report changes; they never rewrite legal explanations.
sources.corrigendaItems: 9 October 2025 corrigendum — Spanish, German, French, Irish, Lithuanian, Hungarian, Slovak, Slovenian and Swedish.
Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 — amendment in force from 27 July 2026.

about.metaDescription: Who publishes The EU AI Act Guide, what it does, what it cannot decide and how children can use it with adult guidance.
about.title: About this guide
about.paragraphs: The EU AI Act Guide is an independent educational demo published by Bencium Limited. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or operated by the European Union, the European Commission or EUR-Lex.

It is designed for non-technical people of all ages. Children may use it, but should involve a parent, guardian or teacher when an AI-related decision may affect their work, education, health, rights or access to a service.

The guide turns selected answers into cautious issue-spotting signals. It does not decide the complete facts, classify a system formally, certify an organisation or replace advice from a qualified professional.
English is the authored source. The other 23 language versions are unreviewed AI-generated demo translations and may contain errors. The selected-language official legal text remains authoritative.

terms.sections: These Terms apply specifically to this website and replace the general Bencium website terms for this subdomain. By using the guide, you agree to these Terms. If mandatory law gives you rights that these Terms cannot exclude, those rights continue to apply.

The guide is an independent educational demo. It does not provide legal, regulatory, financial or other professional advice, and it does not create a professional-client relationship. Its questionnaire results are limited to the answers selected.

Bencium Limited does not guarantee that the guide is accurate, complete, current, continuously available or suitable for a particular decision. Check the linked official sources and obtain appropriately qualified advice before acting on a matter that could affect rights, safety, market access or enforcement exposure.
External links are provided for convenience and source verification. Bencium Limited does not control external services or promise that they will remain available or unchanged.

You may use the guide lawfully and without trying to disrupt, overload, misrepresent or falsely present it as an official EU service. Do not remove source, independence or licence notices when redistributing project material.

Website code and the reviewer skill are provided under MIT. Original project explanations are provided under CC BY 4.0. EU documents, metadata, guidance and icons remain subject to their own official reuse terms.

To the fullest extent allowed by law, Bencium Limited excludes liability for loss arising from reliance on the guide or an unavailable service. Nothing excludes liability that cannot legally be excluded, including applicable consumer rights.

These Terms are governed by the law of England and Wales and its courts have jurisdiction, subject to mandatory rights and courts that apply to a visitor. The English project version governs these Terms, subject to mandatory local law.
People of all ages may access the guide. Children should involve a parent, guardian or teacher before relying on a result for an important decision.
privacy.metaDescription: The guide uses no analytics or non-essential cookies. Learn what remains in the page, what lasts for the session and what Vercel processes for delivery and security.
privacy.title: Privacy and Cookies
privacy.sections: The guide has no accounts, contact forms, free-text fields, file uploads, assessment service, advertising or analytics. It does not use cookies, local storage, fingerprinting, session replay or URL-encoded answers.
Questionnaire answers stay only in the page's temporary JavaScript memory. They disappear when the page reloads or the tab closes. They are not sent to Bencium Limited or stored by the project.
The only session-storage values are a manually selected language and whether the no-cookie notice was dismissed. They last only for the current browser session.

The site is delivered by Vercel. Vercel may process basic request and device information, including an IP address, to deliver, protect and operate its infrastructure. The project does not enable Vercel Web Analytics, Speed Insights, Log Drains or third-party observability integrations.
When you deliberately follow an external official-source link, that external website applies its own privacy practices. No questionnaire answer is added to the link.
For a privacy question about this project, contact ben@bencium.io.
disclaimer.metaDescription: The limits of The EU AI Act Guide and why a result cannot provide legal clearance or replace an authoritative interpretation.
disclaimer.title: Educational Disclaimer
disclaimer.sections: Every result is based only on the choices selected during one short path. The guide cannot see contracts, technical documentation, real-world operation, organisational relationships, national rules or facts that were not supplied.
A 'no trigger found' result is not legal clearance. Industry and organisation size alone do not decide whether the EU AI Act applies. A label or disclosure does not make a prohibited AI use lawful.
Other EU, national and sector-specific laws may apply, including data protection, consumer, employment, copyright, accessibility, platform and professional rules.

The project links to official law and distinguishes binding provisions from official guidance and voluntary codes. Only courts and competent authorities can give authoritative interpretations. Obtain appropriately qualified advice for a real decision.

tools.label-content.duties.machine_reada: Provider duty: apply an effective, interoperable, robust and reliable machine-readable mark to generated or substantially manipulated text, image, audio or video, subject to Article 50(2).
tools.label-content.duties.direct_intera: Provider duty: tell people they are interacting with AI, unless this is genuinely obvious in context.
tools.label-content.duties.visible_or_au: Professional-deployer duty: visibly or audibly disclose that a qualifying deepfake was AI-generated or manipulated.
tools.label-content.duties.public_intere: Professional-deployer duty: disclose generated or manipulated public-interest text unless both qualifying human review and editorial responsibility apply.
tools.label-content.duties.emotion_or_bi: Professional-deployer duty: inform everyone exposed to an emotion-recognition or biometric-categorisation system.
tools.label-content.duties.prohibited_us: Separate Article 5 check: a notice cannot make a prohibited emotion or biometric use lawful.

tools.label-content.examples.public_inte: This text was generated or substantially edited using AI.

tools.label-content.next.check-other-rul: Record these facts, then check platform, consumer, copyright, privacy and national rules.
tools.label-content.next.pause-for-artic: Pause for an Article 5 review. Add an Article 50 notice only if the use can proceed.
tools.label-content.next.implement-liste: Apply every listed duty in the stated channel. Test that the notice appears by first exposure.
